rationale: The residual named in the last interpretation was whether buffering the apply channel lets a queue accumulate behind a slow FSM, since that is the configuration in which the client stops throttling itself. The harness now contrasts the two channel configurations with the same 25ms FSM and the same flood, and the local dry run - native feedback only - showed no accumulation in either: the backlog stayed at one entry or zero and the main-loop probe at a few milliseconds or none, because each commit's delivery to the FSM still gates the loop. The experiment is submitted so the residual rests on a retained receipt rather than on that dry run.

scope.description: Two trials on single-voter clusters with a 25ms Apply in both, differing only in the apply channel: trial 0 buffers it (BatchApplyCh, capacity MaxAppendEntries) so a caller can post without waiting, trial 1 leaves it unbuffered. Each trial fires 400 applies without waiting for their futures, and 150ms in times VerifyLeader - answered inside the main loop for a single voter - recording the latency, the apply backlog between the last log index and the last applied index, and whether that backlog exceeded one batch.
assumptions: BatchApplyCh is a documented configuration option, so contrasting it is contrasting supported deployments rather than an artificial setup.
A single-voter cluster removes elections from the picture and makes VerifyLeader a main-loop probe.
Applies are fired without waiting for their futures, which is what lets the FSM fall behind at all; the earlier version that waited measured nothing.
The dry run is native feedback only; the retained execution is what an interpretation would rest on.
excluded: No application read is served, no disk and no network.
Only two channel configurations and one FSM delay are contrasted.
Multi-node clusters are excluded so the probe's path to the main loop is unambiguous.

parameters.trials: trial 0 BatchApplyCh true, trial 1 BatchApplyCh false; both with a 25ms Apply
parameters.recorded_operands: batch_apply_ch, apply_delay_ms, probe_elapsed_ms, baseline_elapsed_ms, probe_error, probe_slower_than_base, flood_applied, index_lag_at_probe, backlog_accumulated

comparisons.description: With a buffered apply channel the backlog behind a slow FSM still stays within one batch, which is the residual the previous interpretation named; a witness would show a queue accumulating.
Control: the unbuffered configuration also keeps the backlog within one batch.

experiment.prefix: Each trial builds a single-voter cluster whose FSM sleeps 25ms inside Apply, with the apply channel buffered or not according to the trial. It times an idle VerifyLeader as the baseline, starts a goroutine that fires 400 applies without waiting for their futures, waits 150ms, times another VerifyLeader and records the backlog between the last log index and the last applied index, then emits one summary event per trial with the delay, the channel configuration, the two timings, the probe's error, the backlog and whether it exceeded one batch.
